institutionName: Institut d'études politiques de Paris (Sciences Po)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: My interest in improving my French. The city. The quality and focus areas of the university.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy, they do a lot to introduce you in the beginning. I missed the introductory week before the start of the semester which I am sure would have helped.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not much, but I did not have the need for it either

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I lived at the Fondation Danoise in Cité Universitaire which was really, really nice and comparatively cheap. 

Apartments are both expensive and hard to come by

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: There is no on campus accommodation.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Online course registration is an absolute mess. It is on a first-come, first-served basis, but permanent master's student have first priority. It is important to register as soon as the platform opens.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: A guide to registrering for registration, but none as to how the registration itself works. I did not look for any.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I had to let go of my 15 highest prioritized classes, so not very.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You need to prepare an extensive list of possible classes beforehand. Also, don't expect anything beforehand. And be wary that time is of the essence when registrering.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The levels vary quite a bit. Overall, however the difficulty levels are not very high, but the learning outcomes are.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Some classes are very "practitioner" focused which results in them being fairly easy, but requiring a lot of work. In this sense, there is a lack of theoretical or critical approaches to course material in most classes.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Developing and Emerging Economies: the Main Issues
- Biodiversity Values and Policies
- Private Sector, Private Security and International Risks
- Preventive Diplomacy and Multilateral Conflict management in Africa
- Histories and Political Economies of Oil: From North America to the Middle East

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed all of the above classes, but for very different reasons. My favorites were Histories and Political Economies of Oil: From North America to the Middle East (excellent professor and critical approach), Developing and Emerging Economies: the Main Issues (fascinating insights into how the world economy works), and Biodiversity Values and Policies (nice with economic approach to "soft topic")

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: COVID tests cost money

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Food in supermarkets was more expensive than I anticipated. So are beers. 

Coffee, wine, and bread are cheap though!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot! But honestly, there is little time for it. And the sport I wanted to play was in the middle of the day which collided with a class.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Any! It is difficult to get in touch with people during the day - so it is nice to meet people after.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: The museums, the cafés, Paris speaks for itself really. But I would recommend venturing out of the city as well. We took the fast-speed train to Marseille for a few days which was a nice change of vibes and scenery

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It is fairly easy if you are respectful and learn just the basic phrases in French. Remember to say bonjour!

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Don't be afraid to talk to people.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The language barrier to the French students who kept amongst themselves. Luckily, there were almost more international than French students

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The language, and hanging out in local spots

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) It takes a lot of work
2) Remember to enjoy where you are
3) The stay is short, so don't think you can do everything in such a short amount of time

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I went to Paris School of International Affairs - and students there are mostly international. If you want to meet mostly French people, consider other options.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Improving languages, new acquaintances, experiencing Paris

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding French friends and getting to speak French

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
